note: Aquitaine held by English crown after Eleanor's marriage to Henry II until end of Hundred Years' War.

_quarry.structural_significance: Eleanor of Aquitaine's inheritance transformed England's continental strategy from a narrow Norman foothold into a cross-Channel empire encompassing half of France; the resulting Plantagenet-Capetian rivalry dominated European politics for two centuries and the eventual loss of Aquitaine (1453) reshaped both England's continental identity and France's territorial consolidation.
